newsitem.title: KENYA: Index rises, supply tight at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Index rises, supply tight at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: For only the second time in November, turnover at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) passed the 50-million-shillings level on Friday while the bourse's 20-share index continued on its bullish trend.
The index gained a further 9.45 points to stand at 3042.06. Turnover was posted at 53.773 million shillings traded on 1,388,140 shares from 6.280 million shillings on Thursday.
General trading firm Kenya National Trading Corporation (KNTC) continued to offload its shares in Uchumi Supermarket, selling 400,000 shares on the three-day special board, at 44.75.
KNTC held about 7.5 million shillings in the supermarket but has to date offloaded about two million shares to offset some of its debts. No one knows how many more it will offer for sale.

Diamond Trust Bank traded some 742,629 shares on the special board at a reserve price of 35. A broker said the stock had been on a downward trend since it converted into a bank from a financial institution on September 21, 1995.
Brokers said the price decline reflected the decrease in investor confidence in local banks in the market, especially those which converted into banks from financial institutions.
That fall in cofidence was accelerated by the collapse of a number of local banks in the market -- such as that of Kenya Finance Bank mid this year.
Foreign investors continued to support prices in Kenya Commercial Bank buying at between 61-61.50, and at National Industrial Corporation buying at 41.25-41.75.
Power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting jumped to 138 from 133, while Standard Chartered Bank gained 25 cents to close at 46.25.

"One reason the index could be climbing is because there is a lack of selling support on some shares in the market, which has made prices rise," a senior broker said. "There is an overwhelming demand for Nation Printers and Publishers shares but there are simply no shares."
Kenya Breweries closed at 51.50 from 51, while Rea Vipingo Plantations was unchanged at 10.50.
